item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Pranav studies the diagram of triangles $PQR$ and $XYZ$. Matching tick marks show $PQ=XY$, $QR=YZ$, and $RP=ZX$.

Which claim correctly decides congruence from those side lengths?

options.A: The triangles are congruent: three corresponding equal side lengths are enough.
options.B: Equal side lengths appear only after congruence is already known, so sides cannot settle it.
options.C: An included matching angle between two of those sides is also required before congruence can be decided.
options.D: Same shape alone is enough even when the three side lengths do not match.
